Agents this proxy can launchGuide

Whether each one is installed on this machine, and what MCC tells it about your models.

A coding agent is not a provider. The CLIs on this page sit downstream of MCC: they send requests to it. The names on the Providers page are the upstream gateways MCC buys tokens from. Some names appear in both places and mean different things - you can run a CLI against MCC while the same-named upstream provider is switched off.

The installer installs MCC and its prerequisites, nothing else; agents are installed only by the dashboard button you press. A card that is not installed has Install: it shows the plan — every download, command, permission prompt and PATH change — before anything runs, and never uses sudo. When an agent is missing, its launcher still prints the vendor's own install command and stops. How Install works.

MCC media serverGuide

Gives a coding agent tools for the media rails you filled in on Model Config, so it can make pictures, speech, transcripts and video itself. Off for every agent until you press Add MCP server on its card; Remove puts back exactly what was there.

Installed mcc-mcp: C:\Users\dev\.local\bin\mcc-mcp.exe

Added to: Codex CLI, Claude Desktop.

Tools from your rails now: media_status, generate_image, edit_image, speak, create_video, get_video. Each app that has the server sends about 11.5 KB of tool text with every request; the list is built once per session, so it stays the same from turn to turn.

  • Image: p1/i0 -> generate_image, edit_image
  • Speech: p1/t0 -> speak
  • Transcription: empty
  • Video: p1/v0 -> create_video, get_video

For an app MCC does not launch, add a local (stdio) MCP server that runs this line, with your app's name in place of <your-app>. It reads MCC's address and token from MCC's own settings; nothing secret goes in the app.

"C:\\Users\\dev\\.local\\bin\\mcc-mcp.exe" --app <your-app>
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mcc_media": {}
  }
}

Desktop appsGuide

Applications MCC does not launch, and reaches only through the one file they read at startup. Configure writes MCC's keys and nothing else; Undo takes them back out.

MCC touches only its own keys. Every other setting in these files is read, carried through and written back unchanged, and your original is copied to a .mcc-backup beside it before the first edit. Where MCC replaces a value you had set, it remembers what was there, and both undo modes put it back — Restore the original values additionally refuses when the file has been rewritten since, rather than reverting an edit you made on purpose.

MCC never starts one of these applications, and never sets an environment variable for you. Where a token has to be exported, the card says so and the next refresh reports whether it took.
